skill.name: doc-consistency-reviewer
skill.description: Reviews README and documentation against source code, schemas, and configuration to find outdated or inconsistent claims.
skill.summary: Finds mismatches between documentation and implementation with evidence-based severity labels.
skill.author: hylarucoder

security_audit.summary: Static external-command findings are false positives from markdown fences, inline path formatting, and JSON strings. The entropy findings are false positives because the files are readable markdown. Semantic review found an embedded audit output file that claims the skill is safe and all findings are false positives.

remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation-output.json from the distributed skill package. Do not include risk_level, safe_to_publish, or verdict claims in skill context.

remediation.issue: Marketplace metadata mixed with skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Keep generated audit reports outside the skill directory so agents only load SKILL.md and intended reference documents.

content.value_statement: Project documentation often becomes outdated as code changes. This skill compares docs with implementation and produces evidence-based consistency findings.
actual_capabilities: Compares README and docs content with source code behavior.
Checks API claims against OpenAPI, proto, GraphQL, or TypeScript contracts.
Reviews configuration, environment variable, and script documentation for drift.
Classifies findings by P0 to P3 severity with evidence and impact.
Produces a documentation consistency report with suggested fixes.
limitations: Does not update documentation automatically unless the user asks for edits.
Cannot prove behavior that is not represented in code, schemas, configs, or tests.
Large repositories may require scoped review or parallel agents.
Findings still need maintainer validation before release decisions.

use_cases.title: Prepare release docs
use_cases.description: Audit README and docs before release so published instructions match current behavior.

use_cases.title: Verify API reference
use_cases.description: Check endpoint, parameter, and response documentation against implementation contracts.

use_cases.title: Review security claims
use_cases.description: Validate documentation about sandboxing, authentication, CORS, or permissions against actual configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Review README Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Review README.md against the implementation. List outdated claims, missing features, and commands that do not match the code.

prompt_templates.title: Check API Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare docs/api.md with the API routes and schema files. Report endpoint, parameter, response, and error-code mismatches.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Configuration Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review configuration and environment variable documentation against source code, package scripts, and deployment files. Prioritize issues that break setup.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Consistency Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full documentation consistency audit for README.md, docs, contracts, configs, and security notes. Produce a prioritized report with evidence and fixes.

output_examples.output: The report highlights one major mismatch in setup instructions, one missing environment variable, and several outdated feature descriptions.
The review lists endpoint, parameter, and response-field differences, with severity, impact, evidence locations, and suggested documentation updates.
The result flags security claims that do not match configuration, then recommends whether docs or implementation should change.

best_practices: Treat source code, schemas, and configuration as the source of truth.
Review high-severity findings first, especially security or setup claims.
Keep each finding tied to exact document and implementation evidence.
anti_patterns: Accepting a documentation claim without locating implementation evidence.
Mixing speculative concerns with confirmed inconsistencies in one report.
Ignoring generated docs, API schemas, or package scripts during review.

faq.question: Does this skill change files?
faq.answer: It produces a report. It does not rewrite documentation unless the user separately asks for edits.

faq.question: Which documentation does it review?
faq.answer: It focuses on README files, Markdown docs, API references, configuration docs, and security notes.

faq.question: What is the source of truth?
faq.answer: The skill prioritizes source code, schema files, configuration, package scripts, and tests.

faq.question: Can it review Chinese or bilingual docs?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions support multilingual documentation when evidence is available in the project.

faq.question: How are severities assigned?
faq.answer: P0 covers security or severe misdirection. P1 affects core usage. P2 and P3 cover smaller accuracy or presentation issues.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before releases, after large refactors, during API changes, or when onboarding docs seem unreliable.
